source.notes: Paper prints: Series Z1XYW/2, 'SET~1' (text layer; stored as SET-1), Q.P. Code 31/2/1, 27 printed pages, 39 questions, Maximum Marks 80, Time allowed 3 hours. Session is not printed on the paper. English text is on odd pages (Hindi on even pages). Official answers are from the 31/2/1 section of the Science_English_Medium 'ALL SETS' marking scheme; several marking-scheme equations and diagrams are images and are missing from the extracted answer text (flagged per question). The archive's other Q.P. codes in the 31/1 series (31_1_1, 31_1_2, 31_1_3 - 'Set 1') are scanned image PDFs with no extractable text layer at all (pdftotext returns empty pages), so per the brief's instruction to choose an extractable English/bilingual paper, extraction moved to the next code in Q.P.-code order, 31/2/1, which does have a real text layer and a matching marking-scheme section. Separately, on pages 9 (Q12, Q13, Q14) and 19/23-25 (Q34(a), Q37 OR alternative), the PDF text layer is missing chunks of printed text unrelated to the Hindi/English column split (confirmed present in both -layout and -raw pdftotext modes); this looks like a font/encoding or embedded-graphic issue specific to those spans and is flagged per question rather than reconstructed. Question 6 (electrons in the outermost shell of a non-metal atom) belongs to the 'Periodic Classification of Elements' topic, which is not a chapter in the current rationalised NCERT chapter list for this subject; it has been mapped to the nearest genuinely related listed chapter, 'metals-and-non-metals' (valence-electron configuration is discussed there in relation to metallic/non-metallic character).

questions.text:
(a) Why is it important to prevent oxygenated and deoxygenated blood from mixing in birds and mammals ?
(b) Which animals can tolerate some mixing of the oxygenated and deoxygenated blood streams ? On what factor does the body temperature of these animals depend ?
extractionIssues: Only the total mark (2) is printed; the split between (a) and (b) is not printed on the paper (marking scheme gives 1 mark each).

(b) Amphibians / reptiles; the body temperature of these animals depends on the temperature of the environment.

questions.text: We do not clean ponds or lakes but an aquarium needs to be cleaned regularly. Why ?

questions.text: With the help of suitable chemical equations, list the two main differences between roasting and calcination. How is metal reduced from the product obtained after roasting/calcination of the ore ? Write the chemical equation for the reaction involved.
extractionIssues: Subscripts flattened throughout the equations: ZnS, O2, ZnO, SO2, ZnCO3, CO2, HgS, HgO, CaCO3, CaO, Cu2S, Cu2O, PbCO3, PbO, Hg

officialAnswer.text: Roasting is carried out for sulphide ores; calcination is carried out for carbonate ores. In roasting the ore is heated in excess of air; in calcination the ore is heated in the absence or limited supply of air, e.g. 2ZnS + 3O2 -> 2ZnO + 2SO2 (roasting) / ZnCO3 -> (heat) ZnO + CO2 (calcination) (or the equivalent HgS/CaCO3 or Cu2S/PbCO3 examples). Reduction with the help of carbon: ZnO + C -> Zn + CO. (Alternate: reduction with heat alone, e.g. 2HgO -> (heat) 2Hg + O2, or auto-reduction, e.g. 2Cu2O + Cu2S -> (heat) 6Cu + SO2, or any other correct example.)

(i) What is the first step in the breakdown of glucose during aerobic and anaerobic respiration ? Where does it take place ?
(ii) ATP is called the energy currency of the cell. Why ?
(iii) What is meant by residual volume of air in a breathing cycle ?

officialAnswer.text: (i) Glucose -> Pyruvic acid / Pyruvate, in the cytoplasm. (ii) It is used as fuel for all activities in a cell / ATP is broken down giving rise to a fixed amount of energy which drives endothermic reactions in the cell. (iii) When air is taken in and let out, the lungs always contain a residual volume of air so that there is sufficient time for oxygen to be absorbed and for carbon dioxide to be released / the volume of air present in the lungs after exhalation.

questions.text: Write in sequence the steps for experimental verification of the fact that sunlight is essential for photosynthesis.

officialAnswer.text: A potted plant is taken and kept in the dark for 24 hours to destarch it. Cover a part of a leaf of the plant with black paper to prevent that area from getting sunlight. Keep the plant in sunlight for 24 hours. Pluck the leaf, remove the black paper, boil it in alcohol and dip the leaf in iodine solution for the starch test. The covered part showed no change in colour, indicating that starch has not been produced due to the absence of sunlight. The rest of the leaf turned blue-black, proving that starch is produced during photosynthesis and sunlight is essential for that.

questions.text: Define power of a lens. The focal length of a lens is −10 cm. Write the nature of the lens and find its power. If an object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from the optical centre of this lens, according to the New Cartesian Sign Convention, what will be the sign of magnification in this case ?
extractionIssues: Official answer uses stacked fractions for the power formula; linearised here with '/' from the layout.

officialAnswer.text: Power of a lens: the ability of a lens to converge or diverge light rays falling on it / the degree of convergence or divergence of light achieved by a lens / the reciprocal of the focal length of the lens in metres (any one). It is a diverging/concave lens. P = 1/f(m) = 100/f(cm); P = 100/(-10 cm) = -10 D. Sign of magnification = + or positive.

questions.text: Explain the meaning of overloading of an electrical circuit. List two possible causes due to which overloading may occur in household circuits. Write one preventive measure that should be taken to avoid overloading of domestic circuits.

officialAnswer.text: Overloading: overloading of an electrical circuit happens when an excessive amount of electric current flows through the wires. Two causes: (i) contact between live and neutral wire / short-circuiting; (ii) connecting too many appliances to a single socket; (iii) accidental hike in supply voltage. (Any two) Preventive measure: (i) use wires of proper insulation/proper rating; (ii) do not connect too many appliances to a single socket; (iii) use fuse wires. (Any one)

questions.text: Explain how some harmful chemicals enter our bodies through the food chain. Why is the concentration of these harmful chemicals found to be maximum in human beings ?

officialAnswer.text: Some harmful substances like pesticides are used to protect crops. When these chemicals are washed down into the soil or water bodies, they are absorbed by plants along with water and minerals, and by animals from water. When we consume these food items, the pesticides enter our body. (Alternate: crediting an explanation through the food chain.) As human beings occupy the top level in any food chain, the maximum concentration of these chemicals gets accumulated in them.

questions.text:
(i) List three points of difference between nervous and hormonal mechanisms for control and coordination in animals.
(ii) How are auxins related with the bending of plant shoot towards unidirectional light ? Explain.

officialAnswer.text: (i) Nervous control vs hormonal control (any three): messages are sent as electrical impulses vs chemicals (hormones); carried through neurons vs through blood; nerve impulses produce rapid responses vs hormones produce slow responses; nerve impulses produce short-lived responses vs hormones produce long-lasting responses. (ii) When a growing shoot is exposed to unidirectional light, auxin shifts towards the shaded side. More auxin causes more growth of the shoot on the shaded side, resulting in the bending of the stem towards the source of light.

questions.text:
(i) Name the disorder which a person is likely to suffer from due to the following :
(I) Over-secretion of growth hormone
(II) Deficiency of oestrogen in females
(III) Less secretion of thyroxine
Also name the gland that secretes each of the hormones mentioned above.
(ii) How is the timing and amount of hormone released regulated ? Explain with the help of an example.

officialAnswer.text: (i) (I) Gigantism - Pituitary gland. (II) Delay in puberty - Ovary. (III) Goitre - Thyroid gland. (ii) The timing and amount of hormone released are regulated by feedback mechanisms. Example: if the sugar level in the blood rises, more insulin is produced; as the blood sugar level falls, insulin secretion is reduced.

questions.text:
(a) An object is placed in front of a convex lens of focal length f. If the distance of the object from the lens is 2f, draw a ray diagram to show the formation of the image. Write the value of magnification in this case.
(b) A student has focussed the image of a candle flame on a white screen using a convex lens. The situation is as given below :
Length of the flame = 2 cm
Focal length of the lens = 12 cm
Distance of the flame from the lens = 16 cm
If the flame is perpendicular to the principal axis of the lens, calculate the values of the following :
(i) Distance of the image from the lens
(ii) Length of the image formed
extractionIssues: Official answer for (a) includes a ray-diagram image that is not reproduced in the extracted text.
Official answer partly missing in extraction (figure/equation)
Subscripts flattened: ho, hi

officialAnswer.text: (a) Magnification = -1 (deduct half a mark for not marking arrows in the ray diagram). (b) u = -16 cm; f = +12 cm. 1/v - 1/u = 1/f, so 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/12 cm + 1/(-16 cm), giving v = +48 cm. (i) Distance of image from the lens = 48 cm. (ii) hi = (v/u) x ho = [(+48 cm)/(-16 cm)] x 2 cm = -6 cm; the image is 6 cm in size.

questions.text:
The following questions are source-based/case-based questions. Read the case carefully and answer the questions that follow.
The teacher while conducting practicals in the laboratory divided the students into three groups and gave them various solutions to find out their pH and classify them into acidic, basic and neutral solutions.
Group A – Lemon juice, vinegar, colourless aerated drink
Group B – Tomato juice, coffee, ginger juice
Group C – Sodium hydroxide, sodium chloride, lime water
(a) For the solutions provided, which group is/are likely to have pH value (i) less than 7, and (ii) greater than 7 ?
(b) List two ways of determining pH of a solution
(c) Explain, why the sour substances such as lemon juice are effective in cleaning the tarnished copper vessels.
OR
(c) “pH has great importance in our daily life.” Justify this statement by giving two examples.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) (i) Groups A and B – less than 7
(ii) Group C – greater than 7
(b) pH paper and universal indicator.
(c) • Copper vessel is tarnished due to formation of basic copper oxide.
• Lemon juice being acidic react with copper oxide and the salt formed is washed away.
OR
(c) • An optimal pH is required for digestion.
• Change in pH can cause tooth decay
• Animals and plants defend themselves through change in pH.
• Survival of aquatic life becomes difficult when pH of river water becomes low.
(or any other) (Any two)

questions.text:
The following questions are source-based/case-based questions. Read the case carefully and answer the questions that follow.
All the reproductive methods of living organisms are broadly categorized into two types : 1. Asexual reproduction, and 2. Sexual reproduction.
Asexual reproduction involves the participation of a single parent without the formation of gametes, fertilisation and transfer of genetic material. This method is a common means of rapidly increasing offsprings under favourable conditions.
(a) Name the type of fission that occurs in Leishmania and Plasmodium.
(b) Write one advantage of sexual mode of reproduction over asexual reproduction.
(c) Give reasons why :
(i) Colonies of yeast fail to multiply in water but multiply in sugar solution.
(ii) Rhizopus individuals do not grow on a dry slice of bread.
OR
(c) Name the filamentous structures a student could identify when he collected water from a pond that appeared dark green. How do these organisms multiply ? Explain.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) Leishmania – Binary fission ; Plasmodium – Multiple fission
(b) Sexual reproduction leads to more variations which are useful for ensuring the survival of a species.
(c) (i) sugar solution provides nutrients for growth and multiplication whereas water does not do.
(ii) Moisture is required for the growth of Rhizopus.
OR
(c) Spirogyra
Fragmentation – Spirogyra simply breaks up into smaller pieces upon maturation. Each piece grows into a new individual.

questions.text:
Consider the following electrical circuit diagram in which nine identical resistors of 3 Ω each are connected as shown. If the reading of the ammeter A₁ is 1 ampere, answer the following questions :
(a) What is the relationship between the readings of A₁ and A₃ ? Give reasons for your answer.
(b) What is the relationship between the readings of A₂ and A₃ ?
(c) Determine the reading of the voltmeter V₁.
OR
(c) Find the total resistance of the circuit.
extractionIssues: Ohm symbol lost in extraction throughout (resistor/answer values print as bare numbers, e.g. "resistors of 3 each", "Rp = 3/2").
Subscripts flattened: R1, R2, Rp
Official answer uses stacked fractions; linearised here with '/' from the layout.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Both have the same reading, A1 = A3; both are connected in series. (b) Reading of A2 = 1/4 A, as the current is equally divided among the four identical resistors / A2 = 1/4 x reading of A3 / A2 = 0.25 A / A2 < A3. (c) 1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2 (parallel combination), giving Rp = 3/2; V = IR, so V1 = 1A x 3/2 = 1.5 V. OR (c) Total resistance: R = Rp1 + Rp2 + Rp3 = 3/4 + 1 + 3/4 = 13/4 (approx. 3.25).

figures.alt: Circuit diagram: battery, key and ammeter A1 in a loop with three groups of 3 Ω resistors; voltmeters V1 and V2 across the first two groups, ammeter A2 with a 3 Ω resistor in the third group, and ammeter A3
